channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Discuss Further Development of Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Turkey's Deputy Foreign Minister Ayşe Berris Ekinci. The parties welcomed the results of political consultations and noted the dynamic development of their comprehensive strategic partnership. They also exchanged views on international and regional issues and discussed upcoming bilateral events.

item.title: Reforms Elevating Human Dignity Drive Uzbekistan's Development, Says Senate Speaker
item.description: Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbaeva stated that reforms aimed at elevating human dignity are the main driving force behind Uzbekistan's development. She noted that the country's transformation results are recognized internationally, strengthening its regional and global positions. Narbaeva highlighted the recent World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand as an example of this open policy.

item.title: Belarus and Uzbekistan Transition to Joint Production in Agriculture, BelTA Reports
item.description: Belarus and Uzbekistan are moving from simple exports to joint production and technology transfer in agriculture, BelTA reported. Trade in food products and agricultural raw materials between the countries increased by 40% in January-July. Discussions included expanding cooperation, creating a logistics hub, and joint ventures in breeding and processing.

item.title: AfD's Success in Saxony-Anhalt Elections Signals Political Shift in Germany
item.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party secured a significant victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state elections, winning 43.8% of the vote. The ruling Christian Democratic Union (CDU) received only 17.2%. This electoral outcome has led to discussions about potential coalition governments and the AfD's growing influence.

item.title: Environmental Police Officer Killed While on Duty Confronting Poachers
item.description: An environmental police officer has died while performing official duties. The inspector encountered resistance from individuals engaged in illegal fishing using electric fishing gear. The incident highlights the dangers faced by law enforcement officers in combating environmental crimes.

item.title: US Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases Against Uzbek Som
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has announced the new exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek som, effective September 11. The US dollar's exchange rate has seen a further decrease. This development impacts the country's financial landscape.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits and Preferences for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A seminar in Surkhandarya discussed a presidential decree offering new benefits for entrepreneurs, including a three-year exemption from inspections for small businesses. The decree aims to reduce state interference and strengthen protections for businesses, fostering economic growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes six-month licensing for LED lamp imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a six-month mandatory licensing system for importing LED lamps. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce would issue licenses, requiring prior approval from the Ministry of Energy. This aims to curb uncontrolled imports and support local producers, addressing safety concerns.

item.title: Foreigner detained at Osh airport for alleged cigarette smuggling
item.description: A foreign national was detained at Osh International Airport on suspicion of smuggling a large quantity of Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security reported the operation, conducted jointly with customs officers. A criminal case for economic smuggling has been initiated.

item.title: Tajik company Ayan Capital raises approximately $100 million in London
item.description: Tajik company Ayan Capital has successfully raised approximately $100 million in investment in London. The company was founded in London by co-founders of 'Alif'. Further details were not immediately available.

item.title: Kamchybek Tashiev's Defense Plans Appeal Against Bishkek Court Ruling in 'Letter of 75' Case
item.description: The defense team for former State Committee for National Security Chairman Kamchybek Tashiev intends to appeal the Bishkek City Court's decision in the 'Letter of 75' case. Lawyer Ikramidin Aitkulov stated the ruling is illegal and unfounded, questioning the reclassification of charges.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Discuss Cooperation Development in Minsk
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS member states met in Minsk to discuss cooperation. Delegations from Azerbaijan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, UAE, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on information exchange, existing problems, and solutions for enhancing regional law enforcement collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyz court reclassifies charges, imposes probation in "Letter of 75" case
item.description: The Bishkek City Court reclassified charges in the "Letter of 75" case from "Forcible seizure of power" to "Obstruction of electoral rights." All defendants received a four-year suspended sentence with two years of probation supervision. The original verdict included property confiscation, which is not part of the reclassified charges.

item.title: Azerbaijan International Bank acquires 51% stake in Uzbekistan's Davr Bank for $140 million
item.description: Azerbaijan International Bank (ABB) has purchased a 51% stake in Uzbekistan's private Davr Bank for approximately $140 million. The transaction, valued at 1.646 trillion soums, took place on the Tashkent Stock Exchange. This acquisition marks ABB's entry into the Uzbek banking market.

item.title: Foreign national detained at Osh airport for alleged cigarette smuggling
item.description: A foreign national, identified as R.I.A., has been detained at Osh International Airport on suspicion of smuggling a large batch of Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security (GKNB) reported that a criminal case has been initiated for economic smuggling.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to boost electrical engineering exports to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to significantly develop its electrical engineering sector, aiming to increase production and export volumes. The country has already seen substantial growth, with exports exceeding $1 billion and reaching 65 countries. New products like solar panels and electromobils charging stations are being introduced, with further ambitious export targets set for the coming years.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocates $50 million for copper purchases by electrical engineering firms
item.description: Electrical engineering companies in Uzbekistan will receive $50 million to purchase copper raw materials. Companies will cover 25% of the cost, while "Uzsanoateksport" will finance the remaining 75%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan showcases investment potential at China International Fair for Investment and Trade
item.description: Kyrgyzstan participated in the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen, presenting its investment potential and opportunities for joint projects. The fair is a major global platform for government agencies, businesses, and investors. Kyrgyzstan highlighted priority sectors for foreign investors and opportunities to expand business cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan court reclassifies 'Letter of 75' case, sentences defendants to probation
item.description: The Bishkek City Court reclassified the 'Letter of 75' case from attempting a violent power seizure to obstructing electoral rights. Defendants received four-year prison sentences with two-year probation. The case involved an appeal for early presidential elections. Lawyers plan to appeal the ruling, deeming it unlawful.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan implements unified system for foreign student admissions to boost transparency
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established a state enterprise, the Center for Admission of Foreign Students, to create a unified, transparent, and centralized admission mechanism. This initiative aims to attract more foreign applicants and improve the process from recruitment to support during studies, addressing a decline in foreign student numbers.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Adjust Official Currency Exchange Rate Calculation Method from September 15
item.description: Starting September 15, Uzbekistan will modify its official currency exchange rate calculation. The new method will incorporate transactions from the interbank over-the-counter market alongside exchange trading. This change aims to reflect market dynamics more accurately in the official rate.

item.title: Uzbekistan's National Guard Functions to Be Restructured, Senate Approves Law
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Guard will undergo a restructuring of its primary functions, consolidating public safety, order maintenance, and security tasks. A new law, approved by the Senate, mandates National Guard officers to identify themselves when addressing citizens. This aims to enhance accountability.

item.title: Oryonbank Opens New Branch in Kushoniyon District, Khatlon Region
item.description: Oryonbank has opened its 33rd branch in the Kushoniyon district of Khatlon region, Tajikistan. The bank aims to provide residents with easier access to services like loans and deposits. Officials state the new branch will contribute to local economic development and support entrepreneurs.

item.title: Putin: Migration processes generated 321 billion rubles for Russian budget
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that migration processes generated 321 billion rubles in revenue for the state over the past 1.5 years. Over 60 billion rubles went to the federal budget, and over 250-260 billion to regional budgets. Around 100,000 migrants who committed violations were expelled from Russia.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes land transfer for foreign property buyers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a new law requiring foreigners to transfer land ownership to the state when purchasing real estate. The land would be leased back for up to 50 years. This proposal aims to regulate foreign ownership of land associated with properties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan presents investment potential at China International Fair
item.description: Kyrgyzstan showcased its investment potential at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen. The event provided a platform to present investment opportunities, attract capital, and foster collaboration with international businesses and investors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Criminal Liability for Illegal Underground Tunnels
item.description: Uzbekistan is establishing criminal liability for the construction and use of illegal underground tunnels across its state border. The Senate approved amendments to the Criminal and Criminal Procedure Codes. Senator Qutbiddin Burxonov stated that 12 such tunnels were discovered between 2016-2025, used to smuggle goods worth over $3.7 million and 5 kg of gold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Welcomed 9.1 Million Tourists in First Eight Months of 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan hosted 9.1 million foreign tourists from January to August 2026, a 21.1% increase compared to the same period in 2025. August alone saw nearly 1.5 million visitors. Tourism revenue from services reached $4.6 billion, up 53.5% year-on-year. Significant growth was noted from Asian, US, Russian, and European countries.

item.title: Seven Percent of Kyrgyzstanis Lost Money Due to Cyberattacks, Survey Finds
item.description: A 2025 Financial Literacy Survey by the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan reveals that seven percent of surveyed citizens lost money due to hacking or phishing attacks, up from four percent in 2021. The proportion of respondents who experienced bank card detail theft rose to three percent. Digital financial literacy remains a concern, with 30% unsure how to handle suspicious messages.

item.title: Glaciers in Tajikistan's GBAO Show 1.5-2 Meter Decrease in Level
item.description: An international research expedition in August 2026 on glaciers in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) recorded a 1.5-2 meter drop in ice levels. The study, involving Tajik scientists and Swiss university representatives, aims to assess glacier dynamics and their role in water resource regulation amid climate change.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to establish international transport and logistics center in Sary-Tash
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Investment Agency and Textile Trans LLC signed a memorandum to create the Sary-Tash international transport and logistics center. The project aims to attract $100 million in investment and enhance Kyrgyzstan's role as a trade hub between China, Central Asia, and South Asia.

item.title: Bishkek City Court deliberates on "Letter of 75" case verdict
item.description: The Bishkek City Court has retired to chambers to issue a verdict in the "Letter of 75" case. Previously, the district court sentenced several former officials, including the ex-head of GKNB, to four years with probation. Both prosecution and defense appealed this sentence.

item.title: Bishkek to allow private cars on public transport lanes at night and weekends
item.description: Bishkek has approved new rules for dedicated public transport lanes. Private vehicles will be prohibited from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. At night and on weekends, private cars will be allowed to use these lanes. The municipality plans to install new signs and increase enforcement.

item.title: Ombudsman visits prisons, reports inmates have access to medical treatment
item.description: The Ombudsman visited prisons and reported that inmates have access to medical treatment. Ruhshona Hakimbova is learning English, but it remains unclear why the request for surgery for Pirmuhammadzoda's relatives was denied. The article mentions Pirmuhammadzoda is a journalist.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses inclusive education challenges and teacher preparedness
item.description: Uzbekistan is discussing challenges in inclusive education, with over 132,000 school-aged children with disabilities. Currently, 6,801 children are included in inclusive education, while 17,056 receive home-based education. Experts debated the pace versus quality of reforms and teacher readiness.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Discuss International Cooperation and Information Exchange
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS countries met in Minsk on September 9, 2026. Participants discussed international cooperation among internal affairs ministries and the development of information exchange via Interpol channels. They also reviewed participation in Interpol events aimed at improving the organization's charter and rules.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Head of Tashkent International Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, has been appointed as the manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center on a concurrent basis. This new role adds to her existing responsibilities within the presidential administration.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Keyboard Layout for New Alphabet Letters
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to adapt state information systems to a new alphabet, including letters Ö, Ğ, Ş, and Ç. The Ministry of Digital Technologies is developing a unified technical standard for implementation. Data migration, search, and document circulation systems will be updated to accommodate the new characters.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Manager of Tashkent International Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, has been appointed manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center. She will also coordinate the center's activities, represent it internationally, and participate in personnel decisions. The center, established by presidential decree, will feature special legal and currency regimes.

item.title: UN Expert Calls for Protection of Elderly Rights Regardless of Age or Diagnosis
item.description: An independent UN expert urges a new approach to protecting the rights of the elderly, emphasizing that cognitive impairments do not diminish human dignity or fundamental rights. He warns against ageism and decisions made for the elderly without considering their will, highlighting the difference between brain changes and loss of personhood.
